knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=6 \sin {2 t},\,y=3 \sin^{2} {t},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{7 \pi}{12}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=12 \cos {2 t},\,y'(t)=6 \sin {t} \cos {t}=3 \sin {2 t}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(3 \sin {2 t}\right)}{\left(12 \cos {2 t}\right)} \\  & =\frac{\tan {2 t}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{7 \pi}{12},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\tan {2 \left(\frac{7 \pi}{12}\right)}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=4 \sin {2 t},\,y=6 \sin^{2} {t},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{11 \pi}{12}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=8 \cos {2 t},\,y'(t)=12 \sin {t} \cos {t}=6 \sin {2 t}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(6 \sin {2 t}\right)}{\left(8 \cos {2 t}\right)} \\  & =\frac{3 \tan {2 t}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{11 \pi}{12},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{3 \tan {2 \left(\frac{11 \pi}{12}\right)}}{4} \\  & =\frac{3 \left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)}{4} \\  & =- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=4 \sin {2 t},\,y=4 \cos^{2} {t},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{5 \pi}{6}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=8 \cos {2 t},\,y'(t)=- 8 \sin {t} \cos {t}=- 4 \sin {2 t}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- 4 \sin {2 t}\right)}{\left(8 \cos {2 t}\right)} \\  & =- \frac{\tan {2 t}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{5 \pi}{6},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =- \frac{\tan {2 \left(\frac{5 \pi}{6}\right)}}{2} \\  & =- \frac{\left(- \sqrt{3}\right)}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=t^{2} - 3,\,y=4 t^{5} + t^{3},\,0\le t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=2 t,\,y'(t)=t^{2} \left(20 t^{2} + 3\right).
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(t^{2} \left(20 t^{2} + 3\right)\right)}{\left(2 t\right)} \\  & =\frac{t \left(20 t^{2} + 3\right)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=3,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(3\right) \left(20 \left(3\right)^{2} + 3\right)}{2} \\  & =\frac{549}{2} \\  & =\frac{549}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=2 \sin {t},\,y=\frac{6 t^{2}}{\pi},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi}{4}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=2 \cos {t},\,y'(t)=\frac{12 t}{\pi}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(\frac{12 t}{\pi}\right)}{\left(2 \cos {t}\right)} \\  & =\frac{6 t \sec {t}}{\pi}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{\pi}{4},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{6 \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \sec {\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)}}{\pi} \\  & =\frac{6 \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \left(\sqrt{2}\right)}{\pi} \\  & =\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=2 t + \sin {t},\,y=3 t + \cos {t},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{3 \pi}{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=\cos {t} + 2,\,y'(t)=3 - \sin {t}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(3 - \sin {t}\right)}{\left(\cos {t} + 2\right)} \\  & =\frac{3 - \sin {t}}{\cos {t} + 2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{3 \pi}{2},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{3 - \sin {\left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)}}{\cos {\left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)} + 2} \\  & =\frac{3 - \left(-1\right)}{\left(0\right) + 2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=t + \sin {t},\,y=2 t + \cos {t},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi}{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=\cos {t} + 1,\,y'(t)=2 - \sin {t}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(2 - \sin {t}\right)}{\left(\cos {t} + 1\right)} \\  & =\frac{2 - \sin {t}}{\cos {t} + 1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{\pi}{2},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{2 - \sin {\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}}{\cos {\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)} + 1} \\  & =\frac{2 - \left(1\right)}{\left(0\right) + 1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=t^{3} + 1,\,y=6 t^{4} + 3 t^{2},\,0\le t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=3 t^{2},\,y'(t)=6 t \left(4 t^{2} + 1\right).
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(6 t \left(4 t^{2} + 1\right)\right)}{\left(3 t^{2}\right)} \\  & =\frac{2 \left(4 t^{2} + 1\right)}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=3,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{2 \left(4 \left(3\right)^{2} + 1\right)}{\left(3\right)} \\  & =\frac{74}{3} \\  & =\frac{74}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=5 t^{3} + 1,\,y=6 t^{4} + 4 t^{2},\,0\le t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=15 t^{2},\,y'(t)=8 t \left(3 t^{2} + 1\right).
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(8 t \left(3 t^{2} + 1\right)\right)}{\left(15 t^{2}\right)} \\  & =\frac{8 \left(3 t^{2} + 1\right)}{15 t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=2,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{8 \left(3 \left(2\right)^{2} + 1\right)}{15 \left(2\right)} \\  & =\frac{104}{30} \\  & =\frac{52}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
